Connor —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. The team is excited about Redwood's latency profile and the prefix caching notes you showed. Before we lock anything in, my manager wants a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) so procurement and engineering can align on a concrete evaluation timeline, deliverables, and what will trigger a commercial commit.

High level asks from our side:
- A 4-week evaluation window (with acceptance criteria)
- Clear hardware/throughput assumptions for the POC so we can compare cost to our existing solution
- A proposed commit/discount structure tied to post-eval usage (what counts as a ramp and what discount levels attach)
- Renewal terms / uplift expectations if we hit >2x usage at renewal

Can you send a MAP draft and a short note on pricing scenarios (starter commit and uplift bands)? We have procurement calls next Thursday (6/18).

Best,

Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Pilot and next steps (Helix)

Sara —

Thanks for the clear checklist. I built a concise MAP and attached a version you can share with procurement (MAP_Helix_v2.pdf). Summary below:

- Evaluation period: 4 weeks (6/22–7/19) with staged milestones:
  * Week 0 (onboarding): network validation, test corpus ingest, SOC2 evidence review
  * Week 1 (baseline run): 100k tokens/day, latency and quality baselines
  * Week 3 (stress): throughput ramp to 2x baseline, measure cache hit rate and tail latency
  * Week 4 (acceptance): fixed prompt suite pass rate >= 92% and latency SLOs met

- Commercial trigger: Signed Letter of Commitment (LoC) within 10 business days of acceptance to reserve Dedicated capacity.

- Pricing scenarios (examples tied to MAP milestones):
  1) Starter commit: 10M tokens/month year-1, 12% discount off list, 30-day payment terms
  2) Ramp trigger (if 2x baseline within 90 days): automatic 18% discount applied retroactively to ramped volume, provided signed 12-month commit amendment
  3) Renewal uplift: if usage at renewal >2x prior committed level, standard uplift band applies — negotiated case-by-case; for planning purposes assume a 20–35% uplift over prior commitment level with step-down discounts as volumes increase

- Proposed next steps: sign the MAP, kick off onboarding 6/22, run eval through 7/19, Procurement review 6/18 — I can join that call.

Attached: MAP_Helix_v2.pdf, evaluation-checklist.xlsx

Connor O'Brien

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: RE: Pilot and next steps (Helix) — pricing/commit options

Team — forwarding Helix request from Sara. Procurement wants numbers to review 6/18. Initial thought: go with Starter commit (10M tokens/mo @12%) as the base offer, and provide a clear mechanics doc for the Ramp trigger (2x baseline -> 18% discount + 12-month amendment). Two items I want your input on:

1) Renewal uplift guardrail: Helix explicitly called out "renewal uplift" if they go >2x usage. We need a concrete template for how we quantify uplift and the stepwise discounts. Proposed template: 0–1x = baseline price, 1–2x = -6% unit price, >2x = -12% unit price, with a negotiated uplift cap (no more than 35% increase to committed quantity without advance notice).

2) Banking or credits for overage during ramp window — do we credit partial overage toward the first billing cycle after amendment? My recommendation: pro-rate and credit up to 25% of the billed overage as committed consumption if the amendment is signed within 30 days of ramp. Helps reduce friction.

Can you both review quickly? I’m on the procurement call Thursday (6/18) at 10:00 PT with Helix.

Thanks,
Connor

Evan / Sara —

Thanks for the call and the clarity. Attached is the updated MAP and a worked commercial example (SOW_Helix_draft.docx) that shows three lanes and a renewal uplift worked through with numbers. Quick highlights here so you can share with finance:

- Pricing lanes (net unit price per 1k tokens, illustrative):
  * Starter: Commit 10M/month — 12% discount — $0.85 per 1k tokens net
  * Growth: Commit 25M/month — 18% discount — $0.72 per 1k tokens net
  * Enterprise: Commit 50M+/month — 24% discount — $0.58 per 1k tokens net

- Renewal uplift example (Year 1 commit = 10M/month -> Year 2 observed peak = 25M/month):
  * Baseline renewal ask: Year 2 recommit to 25M/month to secure Growth pricing lane (18% discount)
  * If Helix signs a 12-month amendment within 30 days of peak, retroactive pricing adjustment applies back to the start of the peak month
  * Example effective cost delta vs staying at Starter lane without amendment: ~22% savings in unit price across the ramp period

- Ramp credit mechanics: overage during the 90-day ramp window will be pro-rated and convertible to committed units up to 25% if amendment signed within 30 days — this was accepted by revenue ops as a one-time concession for this MAP.

- SLA exception for ramp: Redwood can agree to a 99.5% availability SLA for the 30-day ramp window contingent on Dedicated capacity reservation and a standard SLA addendum executed at signature.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm the MAP today if possible so we can start onboarding 6/22.
2) We will upload the SOW + DocuSign link; once LoC is signed we will reserve Dedicated capacity and apply starter commit pricing.
